observations: Window air conditioning unit with the rear panel removed.
The internal condenser coils are visible and appear heavily soiled with dust.
The compressor and internal wiring are exposed.
The unit is resting on a tiled floor with blue protective sheeting.
No brand name, model number, or technical specification plate is visible in the photo.

claims.evidence: No photo shows this clearly enough to read.
The unit is shown with the back panel removed, which is typical for a scrap unit, but the internal condition is not fully visible.

claims.claim: Barely used, bought new last year. No fault at all, the motor was never opened. Receipt and warranty card available.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The compressor may be seized or non-functional.
risks.proof: A video showing the unit powered on and the compressor running.

risks.risk: The refrigerant gas may be completely depleted.
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturer's specification plate showing the R-134a or R-12 charge.

risks.risk: The internal fan motor may be burnt out.
risks.proof: A video of the unit running with the fan spinning.

risks.risk: The unit may be a generic or low-quality brand with poor parts.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the brand and model name on the front or side of the unit.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the manufacturer's specification plate (usually on the back or side).
Video of the unit powered on and running.
Photo of the interior of the unit with the panel reinstalled.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
